questions.question: What structures are found inside the cells of plant leaves?
options: Mitochondria only
Chloroplasts
Nuclei only
Ribosomes only

questions.question: In which specific cell structures does the process of photosynthesis take place?
options: Chloroplasts
Vacuoles
Cell walls
Mitochondria

questions.question: What is the function of chlorophyll inside the chloroplasts?
options: To absorb light for photosynthesis
To store water for the plant
To absorb minerals from the soil
To release carbon dioxide into the air

questions.question: Why are most plant leaves very thin?
options: To help water evaporate quickly from the surface
To allow light to pass through to the cells containing chloroplasts
To make them lighter so they do not weigh down the branches
To prevent herbivores from eating them easily

questions.question: How does having a large surface area benefit a plant's leaves?
options: It helps them absorb more light for photosynthesis
It allows them to catch more falling rainwater
It prevents gases from escaping too quickly
It increases the rate of mineral absorption from the air

questions.question: Which gas do plant leaves take in from the air for photosynthesis?
options: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen

questions.question: What happens to the oxygen produced during photosynthesis?
options: It is entirely stored in the plant's roots as food
It is converted into minerals inside the stem
It is released as a gas from the leaves into the air
It is dissolved in water and kept in the vacuole

questions.question: What is the process of taking in and releasing gases through the leaves called?
options: Transpiration pull
Osmosis
Active transport
Gas exchange

questions.question: What are the small holes on the surface of leaves called that allow gas exchange?
options: Pores
Stomata
Chloroplasts
Capillaries

questions.question: By what process do gas molecules move through open stomata?
options: Active transport
Osmosis
Diffusion
Filtration

questions.question: How do producers obtain their food?
options: By absorbing decaying matter from the soil
By making their own food using photosynthesis
By consuming other living organisms
By filtering nutrients directly from rainwater

questions.question: Under what condition can the process of photosynthesis take place?
options: Only in the presence of light
Only in the dark
Only when the temperature is below freezing
At any time, with or without light

questions.question: Which of the following describes the nature of photosynthesis?
options: A single physical reaction that occurs outside cells
A series of chemical reactions that take place inside cells
A mechanical process of filtering air
A simple physical change of water into gas

questions.question: What are the reactants and products of photosynthesis?
options: Reactants: water and oxygen; Products: carbon dioxide and glucose
Reactants: glucose and oxygen; Products: carbon dioxide and water
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose
Reactants: glucose and carbon dioxide; Products: water and oxygen

questions.question: Why do we use a word summary of the reactants and products of photosynthesis?
options: To represent a model of the many chemical reactions involved
To list all the minerals a plant needs to grow
To describe how water moves up through the roots
To explain the physical structure of the leaf's stomata

questions.question: Which of the following groups of things do plants need to stay alive and grow?
options: Only light and water
Light, air, water and minerals
Glucose, oxygen, soil and heat
Soil, shade, carbon dioxide and starch

questions.question: How do plants take in different materials from their environment?
options: They take in light and gases through leaves, and water and minerals through roots
They take in water and gases through leaves, and light and minerals through roots
They take in minerals and gases through leaves, and light and water through roots
They take in all materials exclusively through their roots

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding water, minerals, and plant nutrition?
options: Water and minerals are the food that plants eat
Plants do not need food because they have water and minerals
Water and minerals are not food, but plants still need food to survive and grow
Water and minerals are converted into soil inside the roots

questions.question: Where do plants get their food from?
options: They absorb organic food from the surrounding soil
They ingest food particles from the surrounding air
They do not take in food from their surroundings; they make it themselves
They absorb food directly from water in the ground

questions.question: What type of food do plants make, and how do they use it?
options: They make carbohydrate, using it for growth and as an energy source
They make proteins, using them only to absorb water
They make fats, using them to insulate their leaves
They make minerals, using them to support their stems
